card.name: Points where a dose change comes next
card.fires_on: Small linking words, commas and word endings in dosing instructions, just before the text says to change, reduce, reassess or increase something. Also the word changing or changed itself.

modes.label: Comma or link before an action
modes.description: A comma or small word after a time period or dose, right before an instruction to reduce, withhold or consider a change.
modes.example: Reassess after 2 weeks; if rash does not improve<<,>> consider dose reduction.

modes.label: Change wording itself
modes.description: The verb changing or the word is in a phrase about a dose being changed or switched.
modes.example: Maintain the same total daily dose of sitagliptin and metformin when<< changing>> between sitagliptin and metform

modes.label: Reassess word ending
modes.description: The ending of reassess in opioid risk warnings.
modes.example: assess each patient’s risk prior to prescribing and reass<<ess>> all patients regularly for the development of these

card.writes: It lowers the odds of change-words (change, changing, 更换), so the model avoids repeating them at that spot.
card.plain: It fires where a dosing sentence is about to say what to change or adjust after a set time or at a threshold.
